children: anticipates increasing its wafers produced by the 2nm process by an additional 20% by the end of the year, according to reports.
In August, TSMC indicated it hoped to achieve an output of 100,000 per month. However, it now expects to produce 120,000 per month by the end of 2026, according to Taiwan's

. Despite being in the early stages, TSMC's N2 node already has four times the amount of tape-outs versus its previous N3 node at this point. This suggests demand for the highest-end chips available continues to roll on. The company was producing about 20,000 per month by the end of July.

Wafers developed from the 2nm process should quickly contribute to TSMC's revenue. The N2 node only accounted for 3% of TSMC's revenue at the end of the second quarter of this year, according to TechPowerUp. The 3nm node accounted for 30% of revenue and the 5nm node for 33%. The 2nm node will come with a higher price tag for chipmakers due to a more complex manufacturing process. They are estimated to cost about $30,000 per wafer. The N3 cost about $20,000.

title: TSMC increases 2nm wafer production outlook by 20%: report
